[USER] User wants examples of lead vocalists who started as backup singers and how it helped their careers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Examples of lead vocalists who started as backup singers include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Whitney Houston - Worked as a backup singer for Chaka Khan and Lou Rawls, which helped her develop her voice and confidence.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Stevie Wonder - Worked as a backup singer for The Temptations and Marvin Gaye, which helped him develop songwriting and arrangement skills.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Sheryl Crow - Worked as a backup singer for Michael Jackson and Don Henley, which helped her hone her songwriting skills.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Luther Vandross - Worked as a backup singer for David Bowie and Bette Midler, which helped him develop his vocal style.  
[USER] User is interested in how backup vocals contribute to the overall sound during live performances.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Backup vocals contribute to live performances by providing harmony, rhythm, energy, emphasis, and contrast.  
[USER] User asks if there are downsides to relying too heavily on backup vocals.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Downsides of relying too heavily on backup vocals include overproduction, lack of authenticity, limited mobility, and poor balance.  
[USER] User agrees that balance is crucial regarding backup vocals in live performances and asks if some artists rely too much on them to cover flaws.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some artists may rely too much on backup vocals to cover flaws, but backup vocals can also enhance performance and support the lead singer.  
[USER] User inquires about specific genres of music that rely more heavily on backup vocals.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Genres that tend to rely more on backup vocals include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Soul and R&B - Known for intricate harmonies and extensive use of backup singers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Pop - Features tight harmonies and often uses backup vocals to enhance sound.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Rock - While focusing on lead singers, many rock bands still use backup vocals for a fuller sound.
